title: Say no: where ikke goes
objective: Place ikke after the verb in a main clause.
explanation: “Ikke” (not) comes right after the verb in a normal sentence: “Jeg taler ikke dansk.”, “Hun er ikke hjemme.” If the sentence starts with something else, the verb is still second and ikke usually follows the subject: “I dag arbejder jeg ikke.”
sourceReference: Deepwater original starter course (2026-10-29), written for Echo; teacher review required before publishing.

exercises.feedbackCorrect: Right: ikke comes after the verb.
exercises.feedbackIncorrect: Put ikke after the verb: “Jeg taler ikke dansk.”

exercises.prompt: Add ikke: “Butikken er åben.” (The shop is not open.)
exercises.feedbackIncorrect: Ikke goes right after the verb “er”.

exercises.feedbackCorrect: Right: verb second, then subject, then ikke.
exercises.feedbackIncorrect: Keep the verb second: “I dag arbejder jeg ikke.”

exercises.prompt: Write three true sentences about yourself with ikke, for example what you don't eat or where you don't live.
